generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The use of `assert limit == null;` in `writeTo` is risky. If the application is run with assertions enabled (`-ea`), any attempt to serialize an optimized logical plan (where `limit` has been populated by the optimizer) will trigger an `AssertionError`. While the constructor from stream (#H9HS1) explicitly resets this value to `null`, indicating that the optimization is not preserved across serialization, using a hard assertion here may cause unexpected crashes in environments where assertions are enabled. A safer approach would be to simply omit the field from serialization without asserting its state.

The implementation of the limit pushdown for `MvExpand` uses a non-standard approach by encoding the "outer" limit as a property within the `MvExpand` logical node rather than maintaining it as a separate `Limit` node in the logical plan. While this works because the `Mapper` (#CS0C1) explicitly reconstructs the physical `LimitExec` based on this property, it creates a discrepancy between the logical plan structure and the resulting physical plan. Specifically, the transformation in `#9T1V4` (`MvExpand -> Limit -> Child`) results in a physical plan of `LimitExec (outer) -> MvExpandExec -> LimitExec (inner) -> ChildExec`. This is functionally correct but relies on a tight coupling between the optimizer rule and the mapper.

review_comment: This rule seems to cover more cases than simply LIMIT->MvExpand, which the other rule now covers. Presumably the iterative application of the other rules will cover this scenario already, so this removal is of no consequence. And presumably test coverage will pick this up if that is not the case.
